reuse.why: Every step goes through the existing applyWeekendRule(date, rule): the daily skip, holidays and MM-DD entries are added inside it, and getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and schedule-template all call it.

duplication.why: Weekend/holiday logic is defined once; the only repetition is the per-site look-ahead padding (7+2h, count*7+h, 3+2h) each caller computes to compensate for skipped occurrences.

placement.why: The rule and its holiday predicates live in shared/schedules.ts, the new handler sits beside get-upcoming-dates in server/schedules/app.ts, and parseRecurDate carries the new fields into the schedule data.

scope.why: Changes stay within schedule date handling, its handler, types, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: One definition decides move vs skip vs keep, and schedule-template's redundant outer skipWeekend ternary was removed; callers now must handle a null result and keep their own window heuristics.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No caller checks weekends, holidays or daily frequency itself; all go through applyWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated rule logic; the padding formulas are caller-specific window sizes, not copies of the rule.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gained frequency and holidays; applyWeekendRule gained the daily 'return null' branch (the requested rule variation); no call site bypasses it.
